## Scope

This report describes a synthetic product-analytics exercise. It is not based on production customer data. The original committed scripts generate 5,000 synthetic users and 34,542 sessions. The original saved outputs report 12.62% signup-to-conversion, 31.96% overall M6 retention, approximately 27.9% DAU/MAU, and a retention-model ROC-AUC of 0.5946.

## Provenance note

A separate PDF report dated Nov. 9, 2026 reports 92,072 sessions, 12.94% conversion, 31.26% M6 retention, and ROC-AUC 0.567. The exact data and complete generating pipeline for that run are not present in the current main-branch repository. Those are therefore document-reported values, not reproducible outputs from the code below. Do not combine those figures with the original saved baseline.

## Original baseline reproduction

Run from the repository root:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "pROC", "shiny", "bslib", "bsicons"))
source("scripts/01_simulate_data.R")
source("scripts/02_funnel_analysis.R")
source("scripts/03_retention_cohorts.R")
source("scripts/04_predictive_model.R")
```

The following chunks generate the original baseline outputs.

```{r}
source("scripts/01_simulate_data.R")
source("scripts/02_funnel_analysis.R")
source("scripts/03_retention_cohorts.R")
source("scripts/04_predictive_model.R")
```

## Funnel

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
funnel <- read_csv("outputs/funnel_overall.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
funnel |>
  mutate(step = forcats::fct_inorder(step)) |>
  ggplot(aes(step, pct_of_signup)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2878a8") +
  labs(title = "Original simulated funnel", x = NULL, y = "% of signups") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Cohort retention

```{r}
m6 <- read_csv("outputs/m6_retention_by_cohort.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(m6, caption = "Original baseline M6 retention by cohort")
```

## Model performance

```{r}
metrics <- read_csv("outputs/retention_model_metrics.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(metrics, caption = "Original baseline retention-model metrics")
```

The saved baseline ROC-AUC is 0.5946. This indicates weak discrimination and should not be described as a strong or production-ready prediction model. The original A/B novelty comparison used arbitrary random offsets and is not reported here as an empirical effect.

## Corrected analysis status

The `audit/corrected-r-baseline` branch contains additional scripts for a complete daily DAU calendar, descriptive M6 segmentation, and a separate user-level randomized experiment simulation. It does not yet contain a complete replacement funnel and prediction pipeline, nor the full provenance for the Nov. 9 PDF dataset. See `corrected_r/README.md` on that branch before using those scripts.

## Limitations

- All records are synthetic.
- Power-user segment differences are descriptive, not causal.
- The original prediction model has weak discrimination.
- The independent A/B simulation is a methodology demonstration, not a live product experiment.
- The Nov. 9 PDF's alternate dataset and metrics are not reproducible from this repository snapshot.
